passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and operating results should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. See also "Special Note Regarding Forward Looking and Cautionary Statements" at the beginning of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Overview We are a leading provider of high-performance semiconductors powering data center networking, IoT connectivity and cellular infrastructure solutions and were incorporated in Delaware in 1960. We design, develop, manufacture and market a diverse portfolio of products for commercial applications, addressing the global infrastructure, high-end consumer and industrial end markets. The infrastructure end market includes data centers, PON, base stations, optical networks, servers, carrier networks, switches and routers, cable modems, wireless LAN and other communication infrastructure equipment and has expanded to support AI-driven applications and general compute data center applications. The high-end consumer end market includes smartphones, tablets, smart glasses, wearables, desktops, notebooks and other consumer equipment. The industrial end market includes IoT applications such as connected spaces (smart cities, buildings, factories, facilities and commercial buildings), smart utilities (electricity, water, gas and smart grid), wireless charging, medical, security systems, automotive, industrial and home automation, supply chain management, asset tracking and logistics, analog and digital video broadcast equipment, video-over-IP solutions and other industrial equipment. Our end customers for our silicon solutions are primarily OEMs that produce and sell technology solutions. Our IoT module, router, gateway and managed connectivity solutions ship to IoT device makers and enterprises to provide IoT connectivity to end devices. We report results on the basis of 52 and 53 week periods and our fiscal year ends on the last Sunday in January. Fiscal years 2026, 2025 and 2024 each consisted of 52 weeks. Our fiscal year 2027 will consist of 53 weeks. We remain committed to advancing our role as a leading provider of disruptive platforms that enable our customers to deliver solutions to create a smarter planet. We continue to focus on three secular trends that drive our growth strategy: 1. Enabling a smarter, more sustainable planet through IoT solutions; 2. Addressing the demand for higher bandwidth and performance with lower power consumption; and 3. Supporting greater mobility in an increasingly connected world. The increasing adoption of our LoRa technology for low power wide-area networks is providing connectivity solutions that enable IoT networks to make a smarter, more connected planet. The growing deployment of on-device AI in IoT applications further strengthens this opportunity: edge AI architectures transmit processed insights rather than raw sensor data, dramatically reducing bandwidth requirements and making the long-range, low-power characteristics of LoRa an ideal complement to AI-enabled IoT devices across industrial, security, smart city applications and more. passages.text: Please carefully consider and evaluate all of the information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and the risk factors listed below. If any of these risks actually occur, our business could be materially harmed. If our business is harmed, the trading price of our common stock could decline. See also "Special Note Regarding Forward Looking and Cautionary Statements and Summary Risk Factors" at the beginning of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Risks Relating to Macroeconomic and Industry Conditions Our future results may fluctuate, fail to match past performance or fail to meet expectations as a result of conditions beyond our control, such as general economic conditions in the markets we compete, conditions unique to our industry and the financial health and viability of our suppliers and customers, which may cause our stock price to be volatile. Our results may fluctuate in the future, may fail to match our past performance or fail to meet our expectations and the expectations of analysts and investors as a result of conditions beyond our control which may trigger volatile changes in our stock price. Our results and related ratios, such as gross margin, operating income percentage and effective tax rate may fluctuate for a variety of reasons beyond our control, including: general economic conditions in the countries where we sell our products, including economic slowdowns, recessions, persistent or volatile inflation, elevated interest rates and changes in monetary policy; financial market instability or disruptions to the banking or credit markets, including as a result of monetary tightening, reduced liquidity or other stress affecting financial institutions; geopolitical turmoil, such as the conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine and any sanctions, export controls or other retaliatory actions against, or restrictions on doing business with Russia, as well as any resulting disruption, instability or volatility in the global markets and industries resulting from such conflict; the availability of adequate supply commitments from our outside suppliers; the timing of new product introductions by us, our customers and our competitors; seasonality and variability in the computer market and our other end markets; product obsolescence; the scheduling, rescheduling or cancellation of orders by our customers; the cyclical nature of demand for our customers’ products; our ability to predict and meet evolving industry standards and consumer preferences; our ability to develop new process technologies and achieve volume production; changes in manufacturing yields; capacity utilization; product mix and pricing; movements in exchange rates, interest rates or tax rates, which may be exacerbated by divergent inflation trends and monetary policies across regions; our ability to integrate and realize synergies from acquisitions; the manufacturing and delivery capabilities of our subcontractors; and litigation and regulatory matters. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow has strengthened materially across the trend, funding internal investment and reducing reliance on external financing. Free cash flow covers a meaningful share of debt, and the current ratio sits comfortably above the sector median, indicating solid near-term liquidity. This cash generation is the primary support for the credit.

The debt mix has shifted toward very low-coupon convertible notes, with the weighted-average effective interest rate falling sharply as higher-cost term loans were repaid. This lowers cash interest burden and extends the maturity profile, although the zero-coupon instrument still represents a future refinancing obligation.

key_risks.text: Gross and net leverage remain elevated relative to the semiconductor sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is aggressive. Headroom to the next leverage threshold is thin, so a modest EBITDA decline or incremental debt could push the profile weaker. This constrains financial flexibility.

The debt note discloses a large zero-coupon convertible maturity alongside a smaller fixed-rate convertible due shortly, with no term loans outstanding. Refinancing these instruments will depend on market conditions and could require cash settlement or equity issuance, a concrete refinancing feature that warrants monitoring.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating income currently does not cover gross interest expense, with interest coverage below one time and far under the sector median. However, cash interest is much lower than reported interest expense because the largest note carries a zero coupon, so cash debt service is more manageable than the coverage ratio implies.

Free cash flow to debt is below the sector median but still positive, and operating cash flow covers debt at a moderate level. Liquidity is adequate, with cash and a current ratio above the sector median. The main servicing risk is refinancing the convertible maturities rather than meeting ongoing cash interest.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer is a semiconductor supplier with improving revenue and cash flow, but weak operating profitability and an aggressive indicative financial risk profile. Leverage is high versus the sector, coverage is thin, and the debt structure relies on convertible notes. We view the credit as speculative-grade in quality.

Our forward view is that cash generation should continue to support liquidity, but deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and managing convertible maturities. The narrow headroom to the next leverage threshold means a downturn could weaken the profile. We would monitor refinancing plans and margin recovery as key rating drivers.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流於整個趨勢期間顯著增強，為內部投資提供資金並減少對外部融資的依賴。自由現金流覆蓋債務的相當比例，而流動比率穩居行業中位數之上，顯示短期流動性穩健。此現金產生能力是信貸的主要支撐。
債務組合已轉向極低票息的可換股債券，隨著高成本定期貸款被償還，加權平均實際利率大幅下降。這降低了現金利息負擔並延長了到期結構，儘管零票息工具仍代表未來的再融資義務。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿及淨槓桿相對於半導體行業中位數仍偏高，而指示性財務風險狀況為進取。距離下一槓桿門檻的緩衝空間狹窄，因此EBITDA適度下降或債務增加可能使狀況轉弱。這限制了財務靈活性。
債務附註披露了一筆大額零票息可換股債券到期，同時有一筆較小額的定息可換股債券即將到期，且無未償還定期貸款。為這些工具再融資將取決於市場狀況，並可能需要現金結算或股權發行，這是一項具體的再融資特徵，值得監控。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運收入目前不足以覆蓋總利息支出，利息覆蓋率低於一倍，且遠低於行業中位數。然而，現金利息遠低於報告利息支出，因為最大筆票據為零票息，因此現金債務償付比覆蓋率所暗示的更為可控。
自由現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數但仍為正數，而營運現金流以中等水平覆蓋債務。流動性充足，現金及流動比率高於行業中位數。主要償付風險在於為可換股債券到期再融資，而非滿足持續的現金利息。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人為半導體供應商，收入及現金流改善，但營運盈利能力疲弱，指示性財務風險狀況為進取。槓桿相對於行業偏高，覆蓋率薄弱，而債務結構依賴可換股債券。我們認為該信貸的質量屬投機級別。
我們的前瞻觀點是現金產生應繼續支撐流動性，但去槓桿取決於EBITDA增長及管理可換股債券到期。距離下一槓桿門檻的緩衝空間狹窄，意味著經濟下行可能使狀況轉弱。我們將監控再融資計劃及利潤率復甦作為關鍵評級驅動因素。
